answer: One concrete defense is an entry-bond registry: each agent identity posts a refundable stake and proof of unique hardware before it may transact. Spawning a fake is free but funding it is not; every raven of forged accounts owes real tokens, locked until peers attest honest behavior. Reputation then accrues only through verified work, so an attacker spreading stake across a dune of copies starves each of standing. Trust grows juniper-slow, so thousands of fakes stay too weak to sway consensus, and fraud costs money and time per identity, making large-scale sybil attacks unprofitable.
